trust_decision.summary: CheckPermissionWithContext decides whether a principal may act on a table bucket, via checkPermission's chain principal==admin -> principal==owner -> hasIdentityPermission -> resource-policy statements -> DefaultAllow fallback; the principal is minted by getAccountID (reflection over the identity struct) and DefaultAllow is whatever bool each handler hands in.

landing_point.why: The summary names enumeration of administrator-owned table buckets through the S3Tables/Iceberg management API, so the first stop is the ListTableBuckets handler and the CheckPermissionWithContext gate that is supposed to scope it.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The Iceberg REST catalog is a separate, optional service with its own auth middleware that already forwards the authenticated identity name to the same handler, so an engineer can argue it is a different API surface and needs no change of its own.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: weed shell s3tables.* talks to the filer directly with no S3 auth and passes only an arbitrary -account name, so making the Manager/handler deny unless an explicit permission exists breaks every shell table command; the published fix has to re-open it with SetTrusted(true). The zero-config gateway (IAM not configured) and anonymous access must likewise stay on the open default.

O6_input_shapes: principal from a full identity struct in request context (S3 route) vs identity name only in context (Manager/Iceberg route, no struct) vs no identity at all (zero-config) vs an explicitly anonymous identity
identity with Account.Id == admin but no admin action (must fall back to the identity's own name) vs an identity carrying Admin/s3:*/s3tables:* (must stay admin)
principal source order: JWT claims sub then preferred_username, then Account.Id, then identity name, then the X-Amz-Account-Id header
same operation delivered over three transports: X-Amz-Target RPC, REST-style S3Tables paths, and Iceberg REST catalog paths
table bucket with no policy vs with a bucket policy (default-allow only applies when resourcePolicy is empty)
inline identity actions vs empty actions with IAM policy names / session token (IAM path) vs neither

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Plain S3 ListBuckets (GET /) enumerates every directory under /buckets, which includes administrator-owned table buckets, passing each through the S3 ACL ownership check rather than the s3tables owner check.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: ListBuckets is the ordinary S3 bucket API, not the S3Tables/Iceberg management API; table buckets are not S3 buckets and are already filtered by S3 ownership plus VerifyActionPermission, so the advisory's scope does not cover it.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package (weed/s3api) outside the s3tables handler, reached by a different router

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second Manager.Execute caller that builds a synthetic request with only the identity name (e.g. an admin API client or a maintenance job) and inherits NewManager's open default.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Manager is already constructed this way in three places (shell, admin dash, weed mini), so one more caller that forgets SetTrusted/SetDefaultAllow is a natural maintainer mistake.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another identity field read by reflection (e.g. a new PrincipalArn or token claim) added to getAccountID without updating the admin-collapse rule, or an extra account field consulted before Claims.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: getAccountID already reflects over four different identity shapes and its own comment warns that refactorers must keep the reflection in sync.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second catalog front-end (another transport or a reload path) that builds its own s3tables.Manager without mirroring the gateway's DefaultAllow.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The Iceberg server itself is exactly that pattern, and the fix wires the setting by hand rather than by construction, so the next front-end repeats the omission.
